databaseNamingAlgorithm.typicalLength: 22-24 characters, well under Postgres's 63-byte NAMEDATALEN limit
databaseNamingAlgorithm.sensitiveContentHandling: Branch/worktree identity is folded into the sha256 input only, never embedded raw — no container/database/bucket name or log line can leak a branch/ticket/person name.
databaseNamingAlgorithm.uniquenessUnderParallelMatrix: CI_RUN_ID + CI_RUN_ATTEMPT + process.pid + crypto.randomUUID() composite distinguishes concurrent matrix legs, concurrent CI runs, and concurrent local invocations on the same machine.

portStrategyLocal.mechanism: docker run -p 127.0.0.1::5432 (Docker-assigned free host port, double-colon syntax) then `docker port <container> 5432` to discover the assigned port before constructing DATABASE_URL
portStrategyLocal.raceAvoidance: Docker's own bind already happened by the time the port is queried — no discover-then-bind TOCTOU race, unlike a script that pre-scans for a free port and then races to bind it.

portStrategyCI.mechanism: GitHub Actions service container with a dynamic host-port mapping (`ports: ["5432"]`, no fixed left-hand side), resolved port read via `${{ job.services.postgres.ports['5432'] }}`
portStrategyCI.hostPortExposureRequired: Not required by GH Actions' own job-isolation model (each matrix leg gets its own runner VM) but recommended anyway as defense in depth.

migrationSequence: assert exit code 0 and no reported pending migrations
cleanupSequence: docker rm -f <postgres container> (run from a finally/trap-equivalent block, unconditional on test exit code)
no volume was ever mounted, so removal is total — no orphaned data directory can remain

staleResourcePolicy.scope: local/worktree only — CI runner destruction already handles the CI case
staleResourcePolicy.mechanism: docker ps -a --filter label=noramedi.disposable-runtime=true, filtered by noramedi.created-at age
staleResourcePolicy.safetyConstraint: must filter strictly on the noramedi.disposable-runtime=true label; must never remove an unlabeled container

bucketNamingAlgorithm.runKeySharedWith: same runKey derivation as the Postgres databaseNamingAlgorithm, reformatted with hyphens (S3/MinIO bucket names forbid underscores)
bucketNamingAlgorithm.currentTestCodeGap: fileBackupDbIntegration.test.ts currently hardcodes `file-backup-review-${Date.now()}` — millisecond-resolution, not collision-resistant under concurrent execution, and not overridable via any environment variable today. Adopting this naming algorithm requires a test-code change this design task is not authorized to make (see unresolvedQuestions).

credentialsPolicy.automatedProvisioningDefault: freshly-generated random access key / secret key per run, exported as MINIO_ACCESS_KEY / MINIO_SECRET_KEY, never logged
credentialsPolicy.testFileFallbackDefault: reviewminio / reviewminiosecret — retained only as a manual/ad hoc local-convenience fallback inside the test file itself, never the automated-provisioning default

endpointPolicy.addressingStyle: path-style (forcePathStyle: true, already hardcoded client-side by the test)
endpointPolicy.productionUrlGuard: provisioning must hard-fail if MINIO_ENDPOINT resolves to a non-loopback/non-private host or matches any known production hostname/S3 endpoint pattern

cleanupSequence: no volume mounted, so container removal is the sole load-bearing cleanup guarantee — per-object/bucket deletion in-test is defense-in-depth only, not relied upon, since it is currently absent (confirmed gap, see §4 Q7 of the markdown design)

isolation.parallelWorktrees: Guaranteed by container-per-run: two worktrees each provisioning their own Postgres/MinIO container cannot share connection pools, locks, or storage, regardless of naming-algorithm correctness; naming algorithm additionally prevents any human-visible name collision in `docker ps`/logs.
isolation.parallelCIJobs: Each GH Actions matrix leg/job runs on its own isolated runner VM with its own service containers by default; the naming/labeling contract is defense-in-depth, not the primary isolation mechanism, for the CI case specifically.
isolation.processEnvironment: DATABASE_URL/MINIO_* are exported into the invoking process's environment only, immediately before test invocation, never written to a committed .env file; no test file constructs or overrides these values itself (confirmed by direct read of dbVerificationHarness.ts and fileBackupDbIntegration.test.ts, and by F1-002-P2's grep pass over the remaining 20 DB-dependent files).
isolation.externalNetwork: Zero live external-provider calls found anywhere in the 105-file backend + 9-file frontend suite (F1-002-P2 finding, relied upon not re-derived). This design recommends, as a not-yet-implemented defense-in-depth control, a shared test-bootstrap fetch/undici dispatcher override allow-listing only the resolved DATABASE_URL/MINIO_ENDPOINT hosts plus loopback, and recommends restricting CI-runner egress to the npm registry, GitHub, and loopback for any disposable-runtime-backed job.
isolation.productionUrlGuards: NEW, not-yet-implemented control this design specifies: before any provisioning command runs, DATABASE_URL and MINIO_ENDPOINT must be checked against a hostname denylist/allowlist (reject any non-loopback/non-private host, any host matching known production patterns such as noramedi.com or a real AWS/S3 endpoint) — hard stop, not a warning, on a match. No such guard exists anywhere in the repository today (confirmed by this task's own read of db.ts's callers and every DB-dependent test file's own connection logic).

migrationProfiles.name: Empty-database migrate-deploy validation
migrationProfiles.description: Fresh container/database, `prisma migrate deploy` from zero, assert exit 0 and `migrate status` reports up to date, assert all migrations applied (dynamic count read at run time, not hardcoded — 67 migration directories as of this task's own count, expected to grow).

migrationProfiles.name: Previous-release-to-current upgrade validation
migrationProfiles.description: Provision a database at a prior tagged commit's migration set, migrate deploy to that point, then migrate deploy again against current HEAD's full migration set; assert clean incremental apply. Mirrors F0-011-P2's Part B methodology.

migrationProfiles.name: Migration idempotency/status validation
migrationProfiles.description: Run `prisma migrate deploy` twice in a row against the same already-migrated database; assert the second run reports zero pending/no-op work and exits 0.

migrationProfiles.name: Application test execution after migration
migrationProfiles.description: The 22+1 DISPOSABLE_POSTGRES/STORAGE_EMULATOR_REQUIRED test files run against the fully-migrated database — the primary 'does the app actually work' gate.

migrationProfiles.name: Destructive rollback rehearsal
migrationProfiles.description: Explicitly separate, opt-in only, never part of default CI. Hand-authored reverse-DDL against a throwaway database seeded with synthetic evidence rows, demonstrating destructive rollback consequences, mirroring F0-011-P2 Part C. Feeds R-070's still-open tooling-gap discussion; does not close R-070.

r070Boundary.restatement: Standard `prisma migrate deploy` is forward-only and is not rollback tooling. This design's default profiles (1-4) never mutate _prisma_migrations directly and never perform a physical schema rollback. Profile 5 is explicitly opt-in, destructive, non-default, and does not introduce any new automated rollback tool.
r070Boundary.explicitNonClosure: This task does not close, mitigate, or narrow R-070. The underlying tooling gap (no drift-detection between _prisma_migrations and true schema state, no documented reconciliation runbook) is unchanged.

failSafeRules.provisioningFailure: FAIL — tests must fail, not skip
failSafeRules.migrationFailure: FAIL — non-zero exit or any reported pending migration after migrate deploy
failSafeRules.readinessTimeout: FAIL — 60s bounded timeout, no indefinite retry
failSafeRules.cleanupFailure: WARN, non-fatal to the already-determined test result; logged loudly; the stale-resource sweeper is the actual backstop, not the per-run script's own exit code
failSafeRules.unknownRuntimeClass: Escalate to full disposable profile / manual-only classification — never silently exclude, never assume safe (mirrors F1-001's own fail-safe design)
failSafeRules.selectorFailureFuture: Fall back to full suite, including full disposable-runtime provisioning for the full suite, not just a partial subset
failSafeRules.missingCredentials: FAIL CLOSED — DATABASE_URL/MINIO_* unset when required must error immediately, never silently skip
failSafeRules.detectedProductionLikeUrl: HARD STOP before any command runs — new guard this design specifies, not present in the repository today
